plan.scope: Developer finite known-pose circular-segment reconstruction from independently generated raw point intensities; no production correction, physical confidence or global-optimization certificate.

matched_criteria.meaning: Predeclared numerical reconstruction targets for matched synthetic data only; not physical tolerances or calibrated uncertainty.

limitations: Fixed centre, chord direction, homography, point detector and supplied Gaussian covariance; only radius, chord fraction and two source levels are fitted.
Independent truth is evaluated by conditional-normal area/slice formulas, with numerical order checks; no production forward probability is used to render observations or held-out truth.
Pixel support is fixed from supplied pose/prior, never changed with candidate geometry. All planned rows and execution failures are retained.
Adverse-source errors are reported without requiring improvement. Exact constant/single-point nonidentification is distinct from giant-radius numerical saturation.
Full source modes give standardized all-pixel least squares; a named proper-projection control separately exposes omitted raw-model mismatch.
Finite grids and local GN refinements can miss smaller basins. No camera measurement, physical recovery or global certificate follows from a successful numerical case.

The historical R10/f=-.6,0,.6 controls retain those supplied finiteD conditions, but use known pose, raw intensities and PSF: extra oracle information prevents interpreting comparison with old half-level contours as general photo accuracy improvement.
The two-pixel active-level control supplies an explicit adversarial observation vector; its radius is a reference geometry, not a claimed generative truth for that noisy vector.

Complete-boundary discrepancy samples independently specified source arcs/chords and uses analytic point-to-boundary distances. It is not a certified continuous Hausdorff enclosure.

Held-out pixel predictions and objective recomputation use the independent area/slice oracle. Quadrature agreement and engineering cost guards are not formal interval or physical-confidence certificates.
Adverse-source rows retain geometry shifts and held-out errors without requiring improvement. Tiny matched-model errors do not establish robustness to those failures or identify a real camera model.
